body.heading: Collect together
paragraphs: Go outside with your adult and look for fallen leaves on the ground. Pick up leaves that have already fallen. Choose ones with bumpy lines you can feel with your fingers.
Look at each leaf together. Some are round, some are long, and some have pointy edges. Only take a few, and leave the rest for the insects and the soil.

body.heading: Make the picture appear
paragraphs: Put a leaf under a sheet of paper, bumpy side up. Hold the paper still and rub the side of a crayon gently over the top.
The leaf's lines will slowly appear, like magic. Try again with a different leaf or a different colour. Every rubbing is a little bit different.

body.heading: Wonder about it
paragraphs: The lines in a leaf are called veins. They carry water around the leaf, a bit like tiny pipes.
Put two rubbings side by side. How are the veins the same? How are they different? There are no wrong answers, only things you noticed.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: make leaf pictures appear like magic with paper and a crayon.

safetyNotes: Only collect fallen leaves in a safe place away from roads, and wash hands after handling leaves.
Do not eat any leaves or berries, and let your adult check anything you pick up.
screenFreeExtension: Make a rubbing card and give it to someone you like, or press a favourite leaf inside a heavy book to keep.
takeaway: A crayon and paper can show the hidden pattern inside a leaf.
